entries.sanskrit:
तृतीये भूमि-गीतैश् च राज्य-दोषादि वर्ण्यते ।

कलौ च दोष-भूयिष्ठे दोष-हन्त्री हरेर् नतिः ॥

देहेऽहन्तां भूमौ च ममतां कुर्वन्त्य् अतोऽबुद्धा इत्य् उक्तं तद् एव भूमि-गीतैः प्रपञ्चयति—दृष्ट्वेत्य्-आदि । आत्मनि पृथिव्या जये व्यग्रान् उद्युक्तान् । हास-प्रकारम् एवाह—अहो इति । मा माम् ॥१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वात्मनि जये व्यग्रान् नृपान् हसति भूर् इयम् ।  
अहो मा विजिगीषन्ति मृत्योः क्रीडनका नृपाः ॥
word_for_word: faults of royal rule and the like
bowing to Hari, the destroyer of faults
entries.literal_english: In the Third Canto, faults of royal rule and the like are described through the songs of the Earth. In Kali, when faults are abundant, bowing to Hari destroys those faults. It was said that the foolish make the body ‘I’ and the earth ‘mine’; the Earth elaborates that very point through her songs. She laughs at the kings who are eager and prepared to conquer her. The manner of her laughter is: ‘Ah! These kings do not seek to conquer me, although I am merely a plaything of death.’
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
dṛṣṭvātmani jaye vyagrān nṛpān hasati bhūr iyam |
aho mā vijigīṣanti mṛtyoḥ krīḍanakā nṛpāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: येन कामेन । फेनोपमे पिण्डे देहेऽतिविश्रम्भिता विश्वासं नीता ये तेषां नरेन्द्राणाम् एष कामो मोघ एव स्यात् ॥२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
काम एष नरेन्द्राणां मोघः स्याद् विदुषाम् अपि ।  
येन फेनोपमे पिण्डे येऽतिविश्रम्भिता नृपाः ॥
word_for_word: in a lump comparable to foam
entries.literal_english: The desire of kings is futile, even for those who are learned. The kings placed excessive confidence in a body that is like a lump of foam; therefore their desire for conquest is empty.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kāma eṣa narendrāṇāṃ moghaḥ syād viduṣām api |
yena phenopame piṇḍe ye’tiviśrambhitā nṛpāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: कामम् एव दर्शयति द्वाभ्याम्—पूर्वम् इति । इन्द्रियार्थ-लम्पटस्य न राज्य-प्राप्तिः स्याद् इति प्रथमम् इन्द्रिय-षड्-वर्गं निर्जित्य, राज-मन्त्रिणो जिष्यामो वशी-करिष्यामः । सचिवा अमात्याः करीन्द्रा हस्तिपाः, तांश् च जेष्यामः । कण्टकान् प्रतिपक्षान् । अस्य अपास्य । “अथ कण्टकान्” इति वा पाठः ॥३-४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
पूर्वं निर्जित्य षड्-वर्गं जेष्यामो राज-मन्त्रिनः ।  
ततः सचिव-पौराप्त- करीन्द्रान् अस्य कण्टकान् ॥

एवं क्रमेण जेष्यामः पृथ्वीं सागर-मेखलाम् ।  
इत्य् आशा-बद्ध-हृदया न पश्यन्त्य् अन्तिकेऽन्तकम् ॥
word_for_word: of one greedy for sense objects
entries.literal_english: He displays the desire in two verses. A person greedy for sense objects cannot truly gain a kingdom, so the king first says, ‘Having conquered the sixfold group of senses, we shall conquer the king’s ministers.’ The secretaries and counselors are the ministers; the great elephants are the elephant-keepers, and ‘thorns’ means opponents. The king intends to remove and conquer all of them.

entries.transliteration:
pūrvaṃ nirjitya ṣaḍ-vargaṃ jeṣyāmo rāja-mantrinaḥ |
tataḥ saciva-paurāpta- karīndrān asya kaṇṭakān ||

evaṃ krameṇa jeṣyāmaḥ pṛthvīṃ sāgara-mekhalām |
ity āśā-baddha-hṛdayā na paśyanty antike’ntakam ||

entries.sanskrit: एवं केचिद् आशा-बद्धा एव केचिन् मां पुनर् जित्वाप्य् अतितृष्णयाब्धिं विशन्ति । तद् एवम् इन्द्रिय-जयेन ये राज्यं साधयितुम् इच्छन्ति ते ऽतिमन्दा इत्य् आह—कियद् इति ॥५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
समुद्रावरणां जित्वा मां विशन्त्य् अब्धिम् ओजसा ।  
कियद् आत्म-जयस्यैतन् मुक्तिर् आत्म-जये फलम् ॥
entries.literal_english: Thus some remain bound by hope, while others, even after conquering me, enter the ocean through excessive thirst. Therefore those who wish to establish a kingdom by conquering the senses are extremely foolish. ‘How much is this conquest of the self?’ The fruit of conquering the self is liberation, not further material conquest.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
samudrāvaraṇāṃ jitvā māṃ viśanty abdhim ojasā |
kiyad ātma-jayasyaitan muktir ātma-jaye phalam ||

entries.sanskrit: अन्तकं न पश्यन्ति इत्य् उक्तं, तद् एवाह—याम् इति । कुरूद्वहेति भूमि-गीतं कथयन् शुकः संबोधयति, “कुलोद्वहाः” इति तु पाठः सुगमः ॥६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यां विसृज्यैव मनवस् तत्-सुताश् च कुरूद्वह ।  
गता यथागतं युद्धे तां मां जेष्यन्त्य् अबुद्धयः ॥
entries.literal_english: It was said that they do not see death; this verse says the same. Śuka addresses the Earth-song as ‘O best of the Kurus’ while narrating it. The reading ‘O descendant of the family’ is easier.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yāṃ visṛjyaiva manavas tat-sutāś ca kurūdvaha |
gatā yathāgataṃ yuddhe tāṃ māṃ jeṣyanty abuddhayaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: “अबुद्धयः” इत्य् उक्तं तत् प्रपञ्चयति—मत्-कृत इति ॥७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
मत्-कृते पितृ-पुत्राणां भ्रातॄणां चापि विग्रहः ।  
जायते ह्य् असतां राज्ये ममता-बद्ध-चेतसाम् ॥

ममैवेयं मही कृत्स्ना न ते मूढेति वादिनः ।  
स्पर्धमाना मिथो घ्नन्ति म्रियन्ते मत्-कृते नृपाः ॥
word_for_word: whose minds are bound by possessiveness
entries.literal_english: He expands the earlier statement ‘the unintelligent.’ Because their minds are bound by possessiveness of the earth, fathers and sons, and even brothers, fight for my sake. Kings quarrel, saying, ‘This entire earth is mine, not yours, O fool,’ and kill one another in rivalry; they die for my sake.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
mat-kṛte pitṛ-putrāṇāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ cāpi vigrahaḥ |
jāyate hy asatāṃ rājye mamatā-baddha-cetasām ||

mamaiveyaṃ mahī kṛtsnā na te mūḍheti vādinaḥ |
spardhamānā mitho ghnanti mriyante mat-kṛte nṛpāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: रामो नाम कश्चिद् राजा । यद् वा, लोक-दृष्ट्या दाशरथिर् एव निर्दिष्टः ॥९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
पृथुः पुरूरवा गाधिर् नहुषो भरतोऽर्जुनः ।

मान्धाता सगरो रामः खट्वाङ्गो धुन्धुहा रघुः ॥
entries.literal_english: Rāma here may be the name of a certain king. Alternatively, from the ordinary worldly perspective, the Daśarathi Rāma is intended.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source. The pinned source carries a variant-reading footnote after the first line; the verse text is preserved without the editorial footnote.
entries.transliteration:
pṛthuḥ purūravā gādhir nahuṣo bharato’rjunaḥ |

māndhātā sagaro rāmaḥ khaṭvāṅgo dhundhuhā raghuḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
तृणबिन्दुर् ययातिश् च शर्यातिः शन्तनुर् गयः ।  
भगीरथः कुवलयाश्वः ककुत्स्थो नैषधो नृगः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
tṛṇabindur yayātiś ca śaryātiḥ śantanur gayaḥ |
bhagīrathaḥ kuvalayāśvaḥ kakutstho naiṣadho nṛgaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: लोकं रावयति रोदयतीति लोक-रावणः ॥११॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
हिरण्यकशिपुर् वृत्रो रावणो लोक-रावणः ।  
नमुचिः शम्बरो भौमो हिरण्याक्षोऽथ तारकः ॥
entries.literal_english: Loka-rāvaṇa means one who makes the people cry, one who causes the world to weep.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
hiraṇyakaśipur vṛtro rāvaṇo loka-rāvaṇaḥ |
namuciḥ śambaro bhaumo hiraṇyākṣo’tha tārakaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
अन्ये च बहवो दैत्या राजानो ये महेश्वराः ।  
सर्वे सर्व-विदः शूराः सर्वे सर्व-जितोऽजिताः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
anye ca bahavo daityā rājāno ye maheśvarāḥ |
sarve sarva-vidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve sarva-jito’jitāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: मयि उच्चैर् ममतां कृत्वा ये ऽवर्तन्त ते कालेन कथावशेषाः कृताः । विभो इति संबोधनं कुरूद्वहेतिवत् ॥१३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
ममतां मय्य् अवर्तन्त कृत्वोच्चैर् मर्त्य-धर्मिणः ।  
कथावशेषाः कालेन ह्य् अकृतार्थाः कृता विभो ॥
word_for_word: having made strong possessiveness regarding me
subject to the condition of mortals
entries.literal_english: Those who exercised strong possessiveness regarding me became subject to mortality and, through time, were reduced to the remnants of a story. ‘O powerful one’ is an address, like ‘O best of the Kurus’.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
mamatāṃ mayy avartanta kṛtvoccair martya-dharmiṇaḥ |
kathāvaśeṣāḥ kālena hy akṛtārthāḥ kṛtā vibho ||

entries.sanskrit: राज-वंशानुकथनस्य तात्पर्यम् आह--कथा इमा इति । विज्ञानं विषयासारता-ज्ञानं ततो वैराग्यं, तयोर् विवक्षया परेयुषां मृतानां वचो-विभूतीर् वाग्-विलास-मात्र-रूपा न तु पारमार्थ्यं परमार्थं युक्तं कथनं न भवतीत्य् अर्थह् । कस् तर्हि पुरुषाणाम् उपादेयः परमार्थस् तम् आह—यस् त्व् इति । नित्यं प्रत्यहम् । तत्राप्य् अभीक्ष्णम् ॥१४-१५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कथा इमास् ते कथिता महीयसां

विताय लोकेषु यशः परेयुषाम् ।

विज्ञान-वैराग्य-विवक्षया विभो

वचो-विभूतीर् न तु पारमार्थ्यम् ॥

यत् तूत्तमः-श्लोक-गुणानुवादः

सङ्गीयतेऽभीक्ष्णम् अमङ्गल-घ्नः ।

तम् एव नित्यं शृणुयाद् अभीक्ष्णं

कृष्णेऽमलां भक्तिम् अभीप्समानः ॥
word_for_word: the purpose of narrating royal dynasties
knowledge of the insubstantiality of sense objects
of those who have passed away
narration of the qualities of the Supreme
entries.literal_english: He states the purpose of narrating the royal dynasties. The accounts are meant to produce knowledge of the insubstantiality of sense objects and then detachment. The words describing those who have passed away are merely verbal display, not an ultimate reality or a statement of something permanently worthy. What is truly to be taken up is the narration of the qualities of the Supreme Lord, which is sung repeatedly and destroys inauspiciousness. One who desires pure devotion to Kṛṣṇa should hear it constantly, every day and repeatedly.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source. The pinned source carries a variant-reading footnote after ‘yat’; the verse text is preserved without the editorial footnote.
entries.transliteration:
kathā imās te kathitā mahīyasāṃ

vitāya lokeṣu yaśaḥ pareyuṣām |

vijñāna-vairāgya-vivakṣayā vibho

vaco-vibhūtīr na tu pāramārthyam ||

yat tūttamaḥ-śloka-guṇānuvādaḥ

saṅgīyate’bhīkṣṇam amaṅgala-ghnaḥ |

tam eva nityaṃ śṛṇuyād abhīkṣṇaṃ

kṛṣṇe’malāṃ bhaktim abhīpsamānaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: कलि-दोषोपचये सति भक्तेर् असंभवं मन्यमानः पृच्छति—केनोपायेनेति । विधम् इष्यन्ति नाशयिष्यन्ति । यथा यथावत् ॥१६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
केनोपायेन भगवन् कलेर् दोषान् कलौ जनाः ।  
विधमिष्यन्त्य् उपचितांस् तन् मे ब्रूहि यथा मुने ॥
entries.literal_english: Thinking that devotion will be impossible when Kali’s faults have increased, the king asks: ‘By what means will people destroy the accumulated faults of Kali? Tell me exactly how.’
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kenopāyena bhagavan kaler doṣān kalau janāḥ |
vidhamiṣyanty upacitāṃs tan me brūhi yathā mune ||

entries.sanskrit: कलि-युगे कः परो धर्म इति बुभुत्सया पृच्छति—युगानीति । ब्रुहीत्य् अनुषङ्गः । आत्यन्तिक-प्रलय-जिज्ञासया पुनः पृच्छति, प्रलय-कल्पयोः संहार-स्थिति-कालयोः । न चायं बहिर्-मुखः प्रश्न इत्य् आह—कालस्येति ॥१७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
युगानि युग-धर्मांश् च मानं प्रलय-कल्पयोः ।  
कालस्येश्वर-रूपस्य गतिं विष्णोर् महात्मनः ॥
word_for_word: of Time in the form of the Lord
entries.literal_english: The king asks to understand the ages and their respective duties, the measures of dissolution and the kalpa, and the movement of the great Viṣṇu, Time in the form of the Lord.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yugāni yuga-dharmāṃś ca mānaṃ pralaya-kalpayoḥ |
kālasyeśvara-rūpasya gatiṃ viṣṇor mahātmanaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: तत्र युग-धर्मांस् तावद् आह—कृत इति । तज्-जनैस् तत्-कालीनैर् जनैः । दानम् अराग-द्वेषतयाऽभय-दानम् । तद् एव प्रथम-स्कन्धे शौच-शब्देनोक्तम् । विभोः संपूर्णस्य धर्मस्य ॥१८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कृते प्रवर्तते धर्मश् चतुष्-पात् तज्-जनैर् धृतः ।  
सत्यं दया तपो दानम् इति पादा विभोर् नृप ॥
word_for_word: held by the people of that age
entries.literal_english: He first states the duties of the ages. In Kṛta, dharma proceeds on four legs and is upheld by the people of that time: truth, compassion, austerity, and charity. These are the four legs of the complete dharma of the Lord.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kṛte pravartate dharmaś catuṣ-pāt taj-janair dhṛtaḥ |
satyaṃ dayā tapo dānam iti pādā vibhor nṛpa ||

entries.sanskrit: तदानीन्तन-जनान् आह—सन्तुष्टा इति । मैत्रा भूत-मैत्री-युक्ताः । श्रमणा आत्माभ्यासवन्तः ॥१९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सन्तुष्टाः करुणा मैत्राः शान्ता दान्तास् तितिक्षवः ।  
आत्मारामाः सम-दृशः प्रायशः श्रमणा जनाः ॥
entries.literal_english: He describes the people of that age: satisfied, compassionate, friendly toward living beings, peaceful, self-controlled, tolerant, self-satisfied, equal-seeing, and generally devoted to spiritual practice.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
santuṣṭāḥ karuṇā maitrāḥ śāntā dāntās titikṣavaḥ |
ātmārāmāḥ sama-dṛśaḥ prāyaśaḥ śramaṇā janāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: अनृतेन सत्यम्, हिंसया दया, असन्तोषेण तपः, विग्रहेण दानम् इति यथा-सङ्ख्यं योज्यम् ॥२०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
त्रेतायां धर्म-पादानां तुर्यांशो हीयते शनैः ।  
अधर्म-पादैर् अनृत- हिंसासन्तोष-विग्रहैः ॥
word_for_word: a fourth of the legs of dharma
entries.literal_english: In Tretā, one fourth of dharma’s legs gradually diminishes. The legs of adharma are falsehood, violence, dissatisfaction, and conflict.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tretāyāṃ dharma-pādānāṃ turyāṃśo hīyate śanaiḥ |
adharma-pādair anṛta- hiṃsāsantoṣa-vigrahaiḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्मोत्तरा ब्राह्मणाधिकाः ॥२१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तदा क्रिया-तपो-निष्ठा नाति-हिंस्रा न लम्पटाः ।  
त्रै-वर्गिकास् त्रयी-वृद्धा वर्णा ब्रह्मोत्तरा नृप ॥
word_for_word: fixed in ritual action and austerity
entries.literal_english: At that time people are fixed in ritual action and austerity, neither excessively violent nor lustful. They pursue the three worldly aims, are learned in the three Vedas, and the social classes are headed by the brāhmaṇas.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tadā kriyā-tapo-niṣṭhā nāti-hiṃsrā na lampaṭāḥ |
trai-vargikās trayī-vṛddhā varṇā brahmottarā nṛpa ||

entries.sanskrit: हिंसातुष्ट्य्-अनृत-द्वेषैर् इत्य् अयं क्रमो न विवक्षितः । धर्मस्यार्धं ह्रसति क्षीयते । अधर्मस्य लक्षणैश् चिह्नैः, पादैर् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तपः-सत्य-दया-दानेष्व् अर्धं ह्रसति द्वापरे ।  
हिंसातुष्ट्य्-अनृत-द्वेषैर् धर्मस्याधर्म-लक्षणैः ॥
word_for_word: in austerity, truth, compassion and charity
entries.literal_english: In Dvāpara, half of austerity, truth, compassion, and charity diminishes. The order in which violence, satisfaction, falsehood, and hatred are listed is not intended as a sequence. ‘Legs’ means the signs or characteristics of adharma.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tapaḥ-satya-dayā-dāneṣv ardhaṃ hrasati dvāpare |
hiṃsātuṣṭy-anṛta-dveṣair dharmasyādharma-lakṣaṇaiḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: यशस्विनः कीर्ति-प्रियाः । क्षत्र-द्विजोत्तराः क्षत्रिय-ब्राह्मण-प्रधानाः ।
entries.main_sanskrit:
यशस्विनो महा-शीलाः स्वाध्यायाध्ययने रताः ।  
आठ्याः कुटुम्बिनो हृष्टा वर्णाः क्षत्र-द्विजोत्तराः ॥
word_for_word: engaged in reciting and studying scripture
classes with kṣatriyas and twice-born foremost
entries.literal_english: The people of Dvāpara are famous and of great character, engaged in reciting and studying scripture, prosperous householders, and the social classes are headed by kṣatriyas and brāhmaṇas.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yaśasvino mahā-śīlāḥ svādhyāyādhyayane ratāḥ |
āṭhyāḥ kuṭumbino hṛṣṭā varṇāḥ kṣatra-dvijottarāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: कलौ धर्म-पादानां तुर्यांशश् चतुर्थांशो ऽवशिष्यते ।
entries.main_sanskrit:
कलौ तु धर्म-पादानां तुर्यांशोऽधर्म-हेतुभिः ।  
एधमानैः क्षीयमाणो ह्य् अन्ते सोऽपि विनङ्क्ष्यति ॥
word_for_word: at the end it will perish
entries.literal_english: In Kali, only a fourth of dharma’s legs remains, while the causes of adharma increase. That remaining portion also diminishes and will finally perish.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kalau tu dharma-pādānāṃ turyāṃśo’dharma-hetubhiḥ |
edhamānaiḥ kṣīyamāṇo hy ante so’pi vinaṅkṣyati ||

entries.sanskrit: शूद्र-दाशोत्तराः शूद्र-कैवर्तादि-प्रधानाः ॥२५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्मिन् लुब्धा दुराचारा निर्दया शुष्क-वैरिणः ।  
दुर्भगा भूरि-तर्षाश् च शूद्र-दासोत्तराः प्रजाः ॥
entries.literal_english: In Kali the people are greedy, of bad conduct, merciless, dry and hostile, unfortunate and full of thirst. The population is dominated by śūdras and servants.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tasmin lubdhā durācārā nirdayā śuṣka-vairiṇaḥ |
durbhagā bhūri-tarṣāś ca śūdra-dāsottarāḥ prajāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: युगानाम् एवं-भूत-वैषम्ये कारणम् आह—सत्त्वम् इति पञ्चभिः ॥२६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सत्त्वं रजस् तम इति दृश्यन्ते पुरुषे गुणाः ।  
काल-सञ्चोदितास् ते वै परिवर्तन्त आत्मनि ॥
word_for_word: in the differences among the ages
entries.literal_english: He states the cause of the differences among the ages in five verses. Sattva, rajas, and tamas are seen in a person; impelled by Time, they change within the embodied self.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
sattvaṃ rajas tama iti dṛśyante puruṣe guṇāḥ |
kāla-sañcoditās te vai parivartanta ātmani ||

entries.sanskrit: मनश् च बुद्धिश् चेन्द्रियाणि च सत्त्वे यदा प्रभवन्त्य् अतिशयेन वर्तन्ते ॥२७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
प्रभवन्ति यदा सत्त्वे मनो-बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि च ।  
तदा कृत-युगं विद्याज् ज्ञाने तपसि यद् रुचिः ॥
entries.literal_english: When mind, intelligence, and the senses strongly prevail in sattva, know that it is the Kṛta age, characterized by interest in knowledge and austerity.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
prabhavanti yadā sattve mano-buddhīndriyāṇi ca |
tadā kṛta-yugaṃ vidyāj jñāne tapasi yad ruciḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: यदा धर्मादिषु भक्तिः प्रीतिः, तदा रजो-वृत्ति-प्रधानं त्रेता-युगम् इति जानीहि ॥२८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यदा कर्मसु काम्येषु भक्तिर् यशसि देहिनाम् ।  
तदा त्रेता रजो-वृत्तिर् इति जानीहि बुद्धि-मन् ॥
entries.literal_english: When people are devoted to fruitive actions and to fame, know, O intelligent one, that the rajas-dominated activity is Tretā.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yadā karmasu kāmyeṣu bhaktir yaśasi dehinām |
tadā tretā rajo-vṛttir iti jānīhi buddhi-man ||

entries.sanskrit: काम्यानां कर्मणां विषये यदा प्रीतिः, तत् तदा रजस्-तमः-प्रधानं द्वापरं जानीहीति पूर्वेणानुषङ्गः ॥२९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यदा लोभस् त्व् असन्तोषो मानो दम्भोऽथ मत्सरः ।

कर्मणां चापि काम्यानां द्वापरं तद् रजस्-तमः ॥
entries.literal_english: When there is attachment to fruitive actions, understand that the age is Dvāpara, predominated by rajas and tamas; this meaning is supplied by connection with the preceding statement.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The source heading uses an underscore variant for 12.3.29; the verse and Śrīdhara block are retained exactly.
entries.transliteration:
yadā lobhas tv asantoṣo māno dambho’tha matsaraḥ |

karmaṇāṃ cāpi kāmyānāṃ dvāparaṃ tad rajas-tamaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: विषादनं दुःखम् ॥३०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यदा मायानृतं तन्द्रा निद्रा हिंसा विषादनम् ।  
शोक-मोहौ भयं दैन्यं स कलिस् तामसः स्मृतः ॥
entries.literal_english: When illusion, falsehood, lethargy, sleep, violence, despondency, lamentation, delusion, fear, and misery prevail, that age is remembered as the tamasic Kali.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yadā māyānṛtaṃ tandrā nidrā hiṃsā viṣādanam |
śoka-mohau bhayaṃ dainyaṃ sa kalis tāmasaḥ smṛtaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: कलि-दोषान् प्रपञ्चयति—यस्माद् इत्य्-आदिना । यस्मात् कलेर् हेतोः । क्षुद्र-दृशो मन्द-मतयः । क्षुद्र-भाग्या अल्प-भाग्यः । महा-शना बह्व्-आहाराः । वित्त-हीना अपि कामिनश् च । स्वैरिण्यः पुंश्-चल्यः । असतीर् असत्यः ॥३१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्मात् क्षुद्र-दृशो मर्त्याः क्षुद्र-भाग्या महाशनाः ।  
कामिनो वित्त-हीनाश् च स्वैरिण्यश् च स्त्रियोऽसतीः ॥
entries.literal_english: He elaborates Kali’s faults. Because of Kali, mortals are small-minded, of little fortune, and great eaters. Men are lustful even when poor; women are promiscuous and unchaste.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tasmāt kṣudra-dṛśo martyāḥ kṣudra-bhāgyā mahāśanāḥ |
kāmino vitta-hīnāś ca svairiṇyaś ca striyo’satīḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: दस्यव उत्कृष्टाः प्रचुरा येषु ते ॥३२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
दस्यूत्कृष्टा जनपदा वेदाः पाषण्ड-दूषिताः ।  
राजानश् च प्रजा-भक्षाः शिश्नोदर-परा द्विजाः ॥
word_for_word: twice-born absorbed in genitals and belly
entries.literal_english: The provinces will be dominated by thieves, the Vedas polluted by heresy, kings will consume their subjects, and the twice-born will be devoted to genitals and belly.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
dasyūtkṛṣṭā janapadā vedāḥ pāṣaṇḍa-dūṣitāḥ |
rājānaś ca prajā-bhakṣāḥ śiśnodara-parā dvijāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: अव्रता विहिताचार-शून्याः । अशौचाः शौच-शून्याश् च बटवो ब्रह्मचारिणो भविष्यन्ति । कुटुम्बिनश् च गृहस्थाः स्वयं भिक्षाटन-परा भविष्यन्ति, न तु भिक्षां दास्यन्ति । तपस्विनो वन-स्था वनं हित्वा ग्राम-वासा भविष्यन्ति । न्यासिनो यतयो ऽतीवार्थ-लोलुपा भविष्यन्ति ॥३३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
अव्रता बटवोऽशौचा भिक्षवश् च कुटुम्बिनः ।  
तपस्विनो ग्राम-वासा न्यासिनोऽत्यर्थ-लोलुपाः ॥
entries.literal_english: Those who should be observant will be without vows, and the brahmacārīs will be unclean and without the prescribed conduct. Householders will become devoted to begging for themselves rather than giving alms. Forest-dwelling ascetics will abandon the forest and live in villages. Renunciants will become extremely greedy for wealth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
avratā baṭavo’śaucā bhikṣavaś ca kuṭumbinaḥ |
tapasvino grāma-vāsā nyāsino’tyartha-lolupāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: पुनर् अपि स्त्रीणां स्वभावम् आह, ह्रस्व-काया इति । कटुक-भाषिण्यो ऽप्रिय-वादिन्यः । चौर्यं च माया कपटम् उरु च साहसं यासां ताः ॥३४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
ह्रस्व-काया महाहारा भूर्य्-अपत्या गत-ह्रियः ।  
शश्वत् कटुक-भाषिण्यश् चौर्य-मायोरु-साहसाः ॥
entries.literal_english: Women will have short bodies, eat much, bear many children, and be without shame. They will always speak harshly, and will be marked by theft, deceit, and reckless boldness.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
hrasva-kāyā mahāhārā bhūry-apatyā gata-hriyaḥ |
śaśvat kaṭuka-bhāṣiṇyaś caurya-māyoru-sāhasāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: किं च, किराटा वणिजः । पणयिष्यन्ति क्रय-विक्रयादि-व्यवहारं प्रवर्तयिष्यन्ति । किं च, सर्वे जना अनापद्य् अपि जुगुप्सितां निन्दितां वार्तां वृत्तिं साधु मंस्यन्ते ॥३५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
पणयिष्यन्ति वै क्षुद्राः किराटाः कूट-कारिणः ।  
अनापद्य् अपि मंस्यन्ते वार्तां साधु जुगुप्सिताम् ॥
word_for_word: even when there is no emergency
entries.literal_english: Low people, the Kirātas, will become merchants and conduct buying and selling. Even when there is no emergency, everyone will consider a despised occupation or livelihood respectable.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
paṇayiṣyanti vai kṣudrāḥ kirāṭāḥ kūṭa-kāriṇaḥ |
anāpady api maṃsyante vārtāṃ sādhu jugupsitām ||

entries.sanskrit: सर्वोत्तमम् अपि पतिं द्रव्य-हीनं भृत्यास् त्यक्ष्यन्ति । पतयश् च विपन्नं रोगादिभिर् व्यापाराक्षमं कौलं कुल-परम्परायातं त्यक्ष्यन्ति । अपयस्विनीर्दुग्ध-दोहाः ॥३६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
पतिं त्यक्ष्यन्ति निर्द्रव्यं भृत्या अप्य् अखिलोत्तमम् ।  
भृत्यं विपन्नं पतयः कौलं गाश् चापयस्विनीः ॥
entries.literal_english: Servants will abandon even the best husband when he lacks wealth. Husbands will abandon a servant who is ruined by illness and unable to work, even if he belongs to the family. Cows that give no milk will be abandoned.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
patiṃ tyakṣyanti nirdravyaṃ bhṛtyā apy akhilottamam |
bhṛtyaṃ vipannaṃ patayaḥ kaulaṃ gāś cāpayasvinīḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
पितृ-भ्रातृ-सुहृज्-ज्ञातीन् हित्वा सौरत-सौहृदाः ।  
ननान्दृ-श्याल-संवादा दीनाः स्त्रैणाः कलौ नराः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
pitṛ-bhrātṛ-suhṛj-jñātīn hitvā saurata-sauhṛdāḥ |
nanāndṛ-śyāla-saṃvādā dīnāḥ straiṇāḥ kalau narāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
शूद्राः प्रतिग्रहीष्यन्ति तपो-वेषोपजीविनः ।  
धर्मं वक्ष्यन्त्य् अधर्म-ज्ञा अधिरुह्योत्तमासनम् ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
śūdrāḥ pratigrahīṣyanti tapo-veṣopajīvinaḥ |
dharmaṃ vakṣyanty adharma-jñā adhiruhyottamāsanam ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
नित्यम् उद्विग्न-मनसो दुर्भिक्ष-कर-कर्शिताः ।  
निरन्ने भू-तले राजन् अनावृष्टि-भयातुराः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
nityam udvigna-manaso durbhikṣa-kara-karśitāḥ |
niranne bhū-tale rājan anāvṛṣṭi-bhayāturāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: पिशाच-सन्दर्शाः पिशाच-सदृशाः ।
entries.main_sanskrit:
वासो-ऽन्न-पान-शयन- व्यवाय-स्नान-भूषणैः ।  
हीनाः पिशाच-सन्दर्शा भविष्यन्ति कलौ प्रजाः ॥
entries.literal_english: The people will be deprived of clothing, food, drink, beds, sexual relations, bathing, and ornaments, and will resemble ghosts.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
vāso-’nna-pāna-śayana- vyavāya-snāna-bhūṣaṇaiḥ |
hīnāḥ piśāca-sandarśā bhaviṣyanti kalau prajāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: काकिणिके विंशति-वराटका-मात्रेऽप्य् अर्थे विषय-भूते । विगृह्य वैरं कृत्वा ॥४१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कलौ काकिणिकेऽप्य् अर्थे विगृह्य त्यक्त-सौहृदाः ।  
त्यक्ष्यन्ति च प्रियान् प्राणान् हनिष्यन्ति स्वकान् अपि ॥
entries.literal_english: In Kali, people will quarrel even over the value of a tiny coin, abandoning affection. They will give up the lives of dear ones and even kill their own relatives.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kalau kākiṇike’py arthe vigṛhya tyakta-sauhṛdāḥ |
tyakṣyanti ca priyān prāṇān haniṣyanti svakān api ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
न रक्षिस्यन्ति मनुजाः स्थविरौ पितराव् अपि ।  
पुत्रान् भार्यां च कुल-जां क्षुद्राः शिश्नोदरम्-भराः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
na rakṣisyanti manujāḥ sthavirau pitarāv api |
putrān bhāryāṃ ca kula-jāṃ kṣudrāḥ śiśnodaram-bharāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: महान्तम् अनर्थम् आह द्वाभ्याम्—कलाव् इति । त्रि-लोक-नाथैर् आनतं नमस्-कृतं पाद-पङ्कजं यस्य तम् । न यक्ष्यन्ति न पूजयिष्यन्ति । पाखण्डैर् विभिन्नम् अन्यथा कृतं चेतो येषां ते ॥४३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कलौ न राजन् जगतां परं गुरुं

त्रि-लोक-नाथानत-पाद-पङ्कजम् ।

प्रायेण मर्त्या भगवन्तम् अच्युतं

यक्ष्यन्ति पाषण्ड-विभिन्न-चेतसः ॥
word_for_word: bowed to by the lords of the three worlds
whose minds are divided by heresy
entries.literal_english: He states a great misfortune in two verses. In Kali, people generally will not worship the Supreme Lord, whose lotus feet are bowed to by the lords of the three worlds. Their minds will be divided and distorted by heretical doctrines.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kalau na rājan jagatāṃ paraṃ guruṃ

tri-loka-nāthānata-pāda-paṅkajam |

prāyeṇa martyā bhagavantam acyutaṃ

yakṣyanti pāṣaṇḍa-vibhinna-cetasaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
यन्-नामधेयं म्रियमाण आतुरः

पतन् स्खलन् वा विवशो गृणन् पुमान् ।

विमुक्त-कर्मार्गल उत्तमां गतिं

प्राप्नोति यक्ष्यन्ति न तं कलौ जनाः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
yan-nāmadheyaṃ mriyamāṇa āturaḥ

patan skhalan vā vivaśo gṛṇan pumān |

vimukta-karmārgala uttamāṃ gatiṃ

prāpnoti yakṣyanti na taṃ kalau janāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं कलि-दोषान् प्रपञ्च्य प्रस्तुतं तन् निस्तारोषायम् आह—पुंसाम् इति षड्भिः। द्रव्य-देशात्मभिः संभवो येषां तान् । चित्त-स्थश् चित्ते स्फुरितः ॥४५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
पुंसां कलि-कृतां दोषान् द्रव्य-देशात्म-सम्भवान् ।  
सर्वान् हरति चित्त-स्थो भगवान् पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
word_for_word: arising from objects, places and bodies
entries.literal_english: Having elaborated the faults of Kali, he now states the means of escape in six verses. The faults of men arise from material objects, places, and bodies. The Supreme Person, situated in the heart and shining in the mind, removes them all.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
puṃsāṃ kali-kṛtāṃ doṣān dravya-deśātma-sambhavān |
sarvān harati citta-stho bhagavān puruṣottamaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
श्रुतः सङ्कीर्तितो ध्यातः पूजितश् चादृतोऽपि वा ।  
नृणां धुनोति भगवान् हृत्-स्थो जन्मायताशुभम् ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
śrutaḥ saṅkīrtito dhyātaḥ pūjitaś cādṛto’pi vā |
nṛṇāṃ dhunoti bhagavān hṛt-stho janmāyatāśubham ||

entries.sanskrit: अयम् एवोषायो नान्य इति स-दृष्टान्तम् आह—यथेति । धातु-जं ताम्रादि-संश्लेष-जातं हेम्नो दुर्वर्णं मालिन्यं तत्र स्थितो वह्निर् एव हन्ति हरति, न तु तोयादि । एवं योगिनाम् अपि विष्णुर् एव, न तु योगादिकम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यथा हेम्नि स्थितो वह्निर् दुर्वर्णं हन्ति धातु-जम् ।  
एवम् आत्म-गतो विष्णुर् योगिनाम् अशुभाशयम् ॥
entries.literal_english: He gives an example: fire within gold destroys the discoloration produced by an alloy; water and the like cannot do so. Similarly, Viṣṇu alone, situated within the self of yogīs, destroys their inauspicious inner disposition; yoga and similar practices do not do so independently.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yathā hemni sthito vahnir durvarṇaṃ hanti dhātu-jam |
evam ātma-gato viṣṇur yoginām aśubhāśayam ||

entries.sanskrit: एतद् एव विवृणोति—विद्या इति । विद्या देव-तोषासना ॥४८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
विद्या-तपः-प्राण-निरोध-मैत्री

तीर्थाभिषेक-व्रत-दान-जप्यैः ।

नात्यन्त-शुद्धिं लभतेऽन्तर्-आत्मा

यथा हृदि-स्थे भगवत्य् अनन्ते ॥
word_for_word: when the Lord is situated in the heart
entries.literal_english: Learning, austerity, breath restraint, friendship, bathing at holy places, vows, charity, and recitation do not produce complete purification of the inner self when compared with the Lord who is situated in the heart. The Lord’s presence is the decisive purifier.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
vidyā-tapaḥ-prāṇa-nirodha-maitrī

tīrthābhiṣeka-vrata-dāna-japyaiḥ |

nātyanta-śuddhiṃ labhate’ntar-ātmā

yathā hṛdi-sthe bhagavaty anante ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्मात् सर्वात्मना राजन् हृदि-स्थं कुरु केशवम् ।  
म्रियमाणो ह्य् अवहितस् ततो यासि परां गतिम् ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. The pinned source has no separate Śrīdhara explanation for this range.
entries.transliteration:
tasmāt sarvātmanā rājan hṛdi-sthaṃ kuru keśavam |
mriyamāṇo hy avahitas tato yāsi parāṃ gatim ||

entries.sanskrit: आत्म-भावं स्व-स्वरूपम् ॥५०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
म्रियमाणैर् अभिध्येयो भगवान् पुरुषोत्तमः ।  
आत्म-भावं नयत्य् अङ्ग सर्वात्मा सर्व-संश्रयः ॥
word_for_word: to be meditated upon by the dying
entries.literal_english: Therefore, O King, with your whole being place Keśava in your heart. While dying, remain attentive to him and thus go to the supreme destination. The Supreme Person should be meditated upon by the dying; he leads one to the state of the self, being the Self of all and the refuge of all.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
mriyamāṇair abhidhyeyo bhagavān puruṣottamaḥ |
ātma-bhāvaṃ nayaty aṅga sarvātmā sarva-saṃśrayaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: इदानीं कलिं स्तौति द्वाभ्याम्—कलेर् दोष-निधे राजन्न् इति ॥५१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कलेर् दोष-निधे राजन्न् अस्ति ह्य् एको महान् गुणः ।  
कीर्तनाद् एव कृष्णस्य मुक्त-सङ्गः परं व्रजेत् ॥
entries.literal_english: O King, although Kali is an ocean of faults, it has one great quality: simply by chanting Kṛṣṇa’s name, a person becomes free from material association and attains the supreme destination.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ |
kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṃ vrajet ||

entries.sanskrit:
तत् सर्वं हरि-कीर्तनाद् एव कलौ भवति नान्यस्मिन् युगे । उक्तं च—


> ध्यायन् कृते यजन् यज्ञैस्-त्रेतायां द्वापरेऽर्चयन् ।  
> यद् आप्नोति तद् आप्नोति कलौ सङ्कीर्त्य केशवम् ॥ इति ॥५२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कृते यद् ध्यायतो विष्णुं त्रेतायां यजतो मखैः ।  
द्वापरे परिचर्यायां कलौ तद् धरि-कीर्तनात् ॥
word_for_word: by meditating on Viṣṇu in Kṛta
entries.literal_english: What one obtains in Kṛta by meditating on Viṣṇu, in Tretā by performing sacrifices, and in Dvāpara by worship, one obtains in Kali by chanting the names of Hari.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kṛte yad dhyāyato viṣṇuṃ tretāyāṃ yajato makhaiḥ |
dvāpare paricaryāyāṃ kalau tad dhari-kīrtanāt ||
